items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Anyway, Ray Brown was the bass player. Joe Pass was the guitar player. Don Abney was the piano player. Jimmie Cheatham was one of the trombone players. It was an all-star band. All the violins and everything. 40 men. I conducted that whole show.

ctx.x: Jon – the lead trumpet player on “The Tonight Show.” Jon [?Faddis]. Anyway, Ray Brown was the bass player. Joe Pass was the guitar player. Don Abney was the piano player. Jimmie Cheatham was one of the trombone players. It was an all-star band. All the violins and everything. 40 men. I conducted that whole show. I had a real problem playing drums.
So your role was musical director? And conductor?

items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: we’d go in the studio and it would be Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, Ben Webster, Flip Phillips, Illinois Jacquet, Johnny Hodges, Charlie Parker, Dizzy and Roy and maybe Charlie Shavers and Oscar Peterson and Barney Kessell or Herb Ellis and myself and Buddy Rich or Louis Bellson.

ctx.x: Norman Granz was a pretty important figure in jazz during those years. Was he a pretty upright guy to work for?

Oh yeah. You know he did a lot of brilliant things. First of all he put jazz into the concert hall. He took it out of the dance hall and put it in the concert hall. He took it out of the night club and put it in the concert hall. He gave people the very best musicians, I mean he got the top people, he always had top people playing for him, and he paid top salaries. I mean he was a tough guy. I remember we would finish a tour and it would be, we’d go in the studio and it would be Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, Ben…
